title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Recent weeks at $12.03 show median 18.5 vs baseline 18.9; prior price hikes show demand suppression. No promotion history at this price.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: No historical precedent; only one past viral event (2026-09-21) with x1.70 vs baseline, but not repeatable. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk to x1.20.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.9. No events are scheduled. The price is raised 6.2% above regular, which typically suppresses demand—past price increases show a median 24% lift in sales only when the discount is deep, but here the price is higher. The product's recent sales (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-05) averaged 18.5 units at the elevated price, slightly below baseline, suggesting price sensitivity. The TikTok trend is a new driver with no historical precedent; noise-adjusted effect is uncertain. Past promotions show a median 52% uplift, but that was at 10–30% discounts; this is a price increase, so promotion uplift doesn't apply. The uplift model’s 1.00 suggests no change, but the price rise and unproven trend require adjustment. We shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence and price headwind.

PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.9 | 5%-95%: 6.2 - 35.5 | 10%-90%: 9.5 - 31.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
